title: Informalisation in Ahmedabad
body: Ahmedabad was a prosperous city whose wealth was based on more than 60 textile mills employing about 1,50,000 workers. Over the years these workers had gained income security: secure jobs with a living wage, social security schemes covering health and old age, and a strong trade union that represented them in disputes and ran welfare activities. In the early 1980s textile mills across the country began to close. In Ahmedabad the closure was long drawn out and spread over about 10 years. Approximately 80,000 permanent workers and over 50,000 non-permanent workers lost their jobs and were driven into the informal sector. The city faced recession and public disturbances. A whole class of workers was thrown back from the middle class into poverty; alcoholism and suicides spread, and children were withdrawn from school and sent to work. (Adapted from Box 6.2 of the NCERT chapter.)
